title: 8.8 Fine-Grained Spatial and Temporal Thermal Profiling of a 16nm CMOS Buck Converter and SoC Load-Current Emulator Using Low-Voltage Micron-Scale Thermal Sensors
problem: Localized thermal hotspots in high-power-density SoCs and 3D systems with integrated voltage regulators create fine-grained temperature gradients (>10°C across 100μm scales), limiting performance and reliability of AI/ML accelerators and special-purpose compute units.
motivation: As compute density grows for AI/ML workloads and heterogeneous 3D integration expands, on-chip thermal monitoring and management becomes critical to prevent localized failures and performance loss.
method: The work develops low-voltage micron-scale thermal sensors for fine-grained spatial and temporal thermal profiling. A 16nm CMOS buck converter and SoC load-current emulator demonstrate the sensor architecture's ability to capture localized thermal hotspot profiles across heterogeneous workloads.
key_novelty: Micron-scale thermal sensors in low-voltage CMOS enable real-time, fine-grained (100μm scale) thermal profiling of high-power-density SoCs.
contributions: Fine-grained spatial thermal profiling method for heterogeneous SoCs
Low-voltage micron-scale thermal sensor design in 16nm CMOS
Validation on 3D-integrated systems with voltage regulators
Runtime thermal monitoring capability for dynamic hotspot detection
primary_theme: On-chip thermal sensing for power management
